title: Every Day: Times and Routines
overview:
Say the parts of the day.
Say the days of the week.
Say what you do every day.
Say when you do it.
functions: Say the parts of the day
Say the days of the week
Say what you do every day
Say when you do a thing
Ask another person about their day
learningPath: Words: times of day and the week.
Patterns: in the morning, and on Monday.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 15. One day, from start to end.
First, the parts of a day.
The morning. The afternoon.
The evening. The night.
Say them with me.
Now the small word that goes with them.
In the morning. In the afternoon.
In the evening. But at night.
Night is different. At night.
Say them with me. In the morning. At night.
Now the week. You know some already.
Monday. Friday. Saturday. Sunday.
Say them with me.
And the word for a day of the week: on.
On Monday. On Friday. On Sunday.
So: in the morning, but on Monday.
Now what you do.
I get up at six.
I wash. I walk to work.
I sleep at ten.
Say them with me. I get up. I wash. I walk. I sleep.
And the three words that hold a day together.
Every day. Today. Tomorrow.
I work every day. Today is Monday.
Tomorrow is Tuesday.
That is Unit 15. Go and tell your day.

grammar.title: In the morning, but at night
grammar.explanation:
Three parts of the day take in.
One takes at.
That one is night.
grammar.rule:
in the morning
in the afternoon
in the evening

at night

I work in the morning.
I sleep at night.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to say you study after work.
1. That is the evening.
2. Evening takes in.
3. Say: I study in the evening.
4. Now say when you sleep.
5. Night takes at: I sleep at night.
grammar.mistake:
No: in the night.
Yes: at night.
It is the only one of the four that changes.
grammar.tip: Three in, one at. Night is the at.
grammar.practice:
Write in or at.
1. ___ the morning
2. ___ night
3. ___ the evening
4. ___ the afternoon
5. I work ___ the morning.
6. I sleep ___ night.
grammar.answers:
1. in
2. at
3. in
4. in
5. in
6. at
Five or six right? Night is the one to remember.

grammar.title: On Monday
grammar.explanation:
A day of the week takes on.
That is different from a part of the day.
grammar.rule:
on Monday
on Friday
on Saturday
on Sunday

But: in the morning, at night

I work on Monday.
I work on Monday morning.
grammar.workedExample:
Your class is on the first day of the week.
1. Monday is a day of the week.
2. Days take on.
3. Say: The class is on Monday.
4. Add a part of the day: on Monday morning.
5. The on stays, and in is not needed.
grammar.mistake:
No: in Monday.
Yes: on Monday.
Days take on. Parts of the day take in.
grammar.tip: Days take on. Parts of the day take in.
grammar.practice:
Write in, on or at.
1. ___ Monday
2. ___ the morning
3. ___ night
4. ___ Friday
5. ___ the evening
6. ___ Sunday
7. ___ the afternoon
8. ___ Saturday
grammar.answers:
1. on
2. in
3. at
4. on
5. in
6. on
7. in
8. on
Six or more right? You can say when a thing happens.

grammar.title: What I do every day
grammar.explanation:
Say your day in order.
Four short lines is a whole routine.
grammar.rule:
I get up at six.
I wash.
I walk to work.
I sleep at ten.

he, she, it → add s
She gets up at six.
He walks to work.
grammar.workedExample:
You want to tell somebody your day.
1. Start at the beginning: I get up at six.
2. Then the next thing: I wash.
3. Then work: I walk to work.
4. Then the end: I sleep at ten.
5. Four lines is enough for a whole day.
grammar.mistake:
No: She get up at six.
Yes: She gets up at six.
He, she and it add an s to the verb.
grammar.tip: Put your day in order, from morning to night.
grammar.practice:
Write the verb with or without s.
1. I ___ (get up) at six.
2. She ___ (get up) at seven.
3. He ___ (walk) to work.
4. I ___ (sleep) at ten.
5. She ___ (wash) in the morning.
grammar.answers:
1. get up
2. gets up
3. walks
4. sleep
5. washes
Four or five right? Washes takes es, not just s.

grammar.title: Today and tomorrow
grammar.explanation:
Two words that hold your week together.
They need no in, on or at.
grammar.rule:
Today is Monday.
Tomorrow is Tuesday.

I am busy today.
I will come tomorrow.

No word before them:
No: on today.   Yes: today.
grammar.workedExample:
You cannot come to work until the next day.
1. The next day is tomorrow.
2. No small word is needed.
3. Say: I will come tomorrow.
4. For this day: I am ill today.
5. Never say on today or in tomorrow.
grammar.mistake:
No: I will come on tomorrow.
Yes: I will come tomorrow.
grammar.tip: Today and tomorrow take no small word.
grammar.practice:
Right or wrong?
1. I am busy today.
2. I will come on tomorrow.
3. Today is Monday.
4. In tomorrow I work.
5. See you tomorrow.
grammar.answers:
1. Right
2. Wrong — I will come tomorrow.
3. Right
4. Wrong — Tomorrow I work.
5. Right
Four or five right? Good.

readings.title: My Day
readings.genre: One person describing a normal day
readings.setting: A flat and a workplace, over one day
readings.passage:
I get up at six in the morning.
I wash and I eat bread.
I walk to work. It is ten minutes.
I start at seven.
I finish at four in the afternoon.
I walk home.
In the evening I study English.
I sleep at ten at night.
Every day is the same.

readings.title: What Do You Do on Sunday?
readings.setting: A staff room, on a Friday
readings.passage:
What do you do on Sunday?
I sleep late.
And then?
I wash my clothes.
In the afternoon I walk in the park.
Do you work on Saturday?
Yes, in the morning.
So Sunday is your day off?
Yes. Only Sunday.

We are closed on Sunday.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The days of the week
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
Monday ... Tuesday ... Wednesday
Thursday ... Friday ... Saturday ... Sunday
Wednesday is strange. It sounds like WENZ-day.
Now say all seven in order.
Tap the mic. Say the seven days.
Check: seven days, in order?
speaking.tutor: Say the days to the tutor. Ask which ones were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — My day
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about your day, in order.
1. I get up at ___.
2. In the morning I ___.
3. In the evening I ___.
4. I sleep at ___.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: in the morning, but at night?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor your day from morning to night. Ask about its day.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say four lines about your day, in order.
One. I get up at ...
Two. In the morning I ...
Three. In the evening I ...
Four. I sleep at ...
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: in the morning, but at night?

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Ask about a day
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: What time do you get up? B: At six. And you?
2. A: At seven. B: What do you do on Sunday?
3. A: I rest. B: Do you work on Saturday?
4. A: Yes, in the morning. B: So Sunday is your day off?
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you ask back each time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor three questions about its day. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — In, on or at?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say in, on or at.
1. the morning
2. night
3. Monday
4. the evening
5. Sunday
6. the afternoon
7. Friday
8. night
Tap the mic. Say eight answers.
Check: in, at, on, in, on, in, on, at.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor when it says in and when it says on.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Today and tomorrow
speaking.instructions:
Say each line out loud.
1. Today is Monday.
2. Tomorrow is Tuesday.
3. I am busy today.
4. I will come tomorrow.
5. See you tomorrow.
Tap the mic. Say the five lines.
Check: no small word before today or tomorrow?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor what day it is today and what day tomorrow is.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The day endings
speaking.instructions:
All seven days end the same way. Listen.
MON-day ... TUES-day ... FRI-day
The first part is strong. The day part is quiet.
It sounds like dee, not DAY.
Now say: Monday, Friday, Sunday.
Tap the mic. Say all three.
Check: is the first part strong?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three days. Say which part was strong.

writing.title: Writing 1 — My day
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your day, in order.
Use in the morning, in the evening and at night.
writing.model:
I get up at six in the morning.
I walk to work.
In the evening I study English.
I sleep at ten at night.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
They are in order, from morning to night.
In before a part of the day, at before night.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line about what you do on Sunday.

writing.title: Writing 2 — My week
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your week.
Say what you do on three different days.
writing.model:
I work on Monday and Friday.
On Saturday I work in the morning.
Sunday is my day off.
On Sunday I rest.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
At least three different days named.
On before every day of the week.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line saying which day you like best.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Which part of the day?
activities.instructions:
Morning, afternoon, evening or night?
1. Seven o'clock, and you get up. ___
2. Two o'clock, after lunch. ___
3. Seven o'clock, and it is dark. ___
4. Twelve o'clock, and everybody sleeps. ___
5. Nine o'clock, and you start work. ___
activities.answers:
1. morning
2. afternoon
3. evening
4. night
5. morning
Four or five right: good.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 2 — The days in order
activities.instructions:
Put them in order, from Monday.
Friday, Monday, Sunday, Saturday
Then answer:
1. What comes after Monday?
2. What comes before Sunday?
3. Which two days do most people not work?
activities.answers:
In order: Monday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday
1. Tuesday
2. Saturday
3. Saturday and Sunday
Four or five right: good.

activities.title: Practice 3 — In, on or at?
activities.instructions:
Write in, on or at.
1. ___ the morning
2. ___ night
3. ___ Monday
4. ___ the evening
5. ___ Sunday
6. ___ the afternoon
7. ___ Friday
8. ___ the morning
activities.answers:
1. in
2. at
3. on
4. in
5. on
6. in
7. on
8. in
Six or more right: good. Days take on. Parts of the day take in.
Night is the one that takes at.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Add the s
activities.instructions:
Write the verb correctly.
1. I ___ (get up) at six.
2. She ___ (get up) at seven.
3. He ___ (walk) to work.
4. I ___ (sleep) at ten.
5. She ___ (wash) in the morning.
6. They ___ (work) on Monday.
activities.answers:
1. get up
2. gets up
3. walks
4. sleep
5. washes
6. work
Five or six right: good. He and she add s. Wash adds es.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Right or wrong?
activities.instructions:
Write right or wrong.
1. I am busy today.
2. I will come on tomorrow.
3. Today is Monday.
4. In tomorrow I work.
5. See you tomorrow.
activities.answers:
1. right
2. wrong (I will come tomorrow)
3. right
4. wrong (Tomorrow I work)
5. right
Four or five right: good. Today and tomorrow take no small word.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read the notice
activities.instructions:
Read Opening Times again.
1. What time does the shop open on Monday?
2. What time does it close on Saturday?
3. Is it open on Sunday?
4. When is the market?
5. How many days is the shop open?
activities.answers:
1. Eight
2. One
3. No
4. Friday morning
5. Six
Four or five right: you can read opening times.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: The first part of the day is the ___.
The dark part, when people sleep, is the ___.
quizzes.why: Night is the dark part of the day.

quizzes.q: How many days are in a week?

quizzes.why: Parts of the day take in.
Night is the one that takes at.
A day of the week takes on.
He and she add an s to the verb.

quizzes.q: Which question asks about a routine?
options: What time do you get up?
quizzes.a: What time do you get up?
quizzes.why: It asks about a thing you do every day.
Today and tomorrow take no small word before them.
Tomorrow is the day after today.

quizzes.q: The day you do not work is your ___.
quizzes.why: A day off is a day with no work.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: In, on and at is arbitrary and must be learned, not reasoned
teacherNotes.note: There is no rule a learner can work out: parts of the day take in, night takes at, days take on. Do not try to explain why. Drill the three groups and let the pattern settle.

teacherNotes.type: Four lines is a whole day
teacherNotes.note: A learner who can say I get up at six, I walk to work, in the evening I study, I sleep at ten has told you their entire routine. That is a real piece of communication at Pre-A1 and it is worth more than the vocabulary list.

teacherNotes.type: Wednesday does not sound like it looks
teacherNotes.note: WENZ-day. Learners who sound out the spelling get it wrong every time. Say it before they read it, which is why Speaking 1 comes before any written list.

teacherNotes.type: The third-person s arrives here quietly
teacherNotes.note: She gets up, he walks. It is not the focus of the unit and it will not stick yet. Correct it, do not dwell on it, and expect Level 1 to teach it properly.

assignment.title: My day and my week
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say four lines about your day, in order.
Use in the morning, in the evening and at night.
2. Write four lines about your week.
Say what you do on three different days.
Listen back before you finish.
